items.headline: Kramatorsk: frontline now ~8 km after Ukrainian counterattacks
items.summary: AMK Mapping: after recent Ukrainian counterattacks on the Kramatorsk direction, the frontline — previously as close as ~3 km — is now about 8 km from the city. Entry into Kramatorsk unlikely for now.

items.headline: Dobropillia completely destroyed — October 2026
items.summary: AMK Mapping posts imagery/note that Dobropillia has been completely destroyed as fighting and strikes continue on the Pokrovsk–Dobropillia axis.

items.headline: Kyiv: South + Patona bridges closed after Geran jet-drone strikes
items.summary: Repeated overnight Geran-4/5 strikes on the South Bridge; traffic closed both ways on South and Patona; Metro Bridge partial closure. Large jams. MoD claim: rail bridge over Dnieper used for Donbas logistics; 750 kV Nalyvaikivka substation also hit.

items.headline: TASS: MoD claims 17 communities taken Sep 26–Oct 2
items.summary: Russian Defense Ministry via TASS: 17 communities liberated across Kharkov, Sumy, Zaporozhye and DPR over the week, including three in the past day. Battlegroup North cited on Kharkov encirclement; precision/UAV strikes on logistics and power.

items.headline: Peskov: lasting peace not ceasefire; Black Sea price for strikes
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman: Russia needs peace not a ceasefire; piecemeal deals won't settle; Ukraine 'must pay' for Black Sea strikes and is already paying as Moscow targets sea logistics.

items.headline: FACTBOX: MoD lists Kyiv bridge, Nalyvaikivka substation, Izmail port hits
items.summary: TASS factbox of claimed strikes: Dnieper road-rail bridge in Kyiv, Kievskaya electrical substation at Nalivaykovka, Izmail port industrial complex, and a cargo ship in the Black Sea. Kyiv city closed multiple bridges to traffic.

items.headline: MS 10.02: 'No more rules' air campaign — bridges, Sumy, Kharkiv pocket
items.summary: Military Summary sitrep: Zelensky intel claim Putin lifts air-campaign restrictions; South Bridge hits and Kyiv gridlock; 750 kV substation; Kostopil/Pavlohrad; Mala Rybytsia (Sumy) claimed fallen; flag over Vysoka Yaruga; Kharkiv cauldron narrative.

items.headline: Anzalone: Russia's nuclear threats — is NATO provoking war?
items.summary: Kyle Anzalone Show short on Russian nuclear signaling and NATO escalation risk — Mercouris-adjacent antiwar framing on the European theater.

items.headline: Moon of Alabama: Ukraine Open Thread 2026-215
items.summary: b's open thread for Ukraine war news & views — standing Mercouris-cited blog for attrition/diplomacy commentary.

items.headline: FT (via Zelenskyy): Putin told military to abandon 'rules of war'
items.summary: Major FT-circulated headline only: Zelenskyy claims Putin ordered abandonment of wartime restrictions — paired on desk with MS 'no more rules' air-campaign framing. Mainstream exception.

items.headline: Diesen × Sachs: Ukraine peace proposal vs NATO salami tactics
items.summary: Glenn Diesen hosts Jeffrey Sachs on peace terms versus incremental NATO escalation — desk lens: negotiate neutrality/limits, don’t salami-slice Russia into a wider war.

items.headline: Desk frame: Horton’s Provoked — NATO expansion made this war
items.summary: Standing shelf: Provoked: How Washington Started the New Cold War with Russia and the Catastrophe in Ukraine. Desk voice starts from broken assurances / NATO creep / proxy design — not “unprovoked.”

items.headline: MS: Nesterne, Rublene & Vysoka Yaruha claimed fallen
items.summary: Short MS update aligning with TASS Battlegroup North claims on three Kharkiv-region settlements inside/near the northeastern pocket.

items.headline: Antiwar News w/ DeCamp: Senate kills Israel-US citizens report bill + Somalia strikes
items.summary: Daily DeCamp wire (Antiwar News). Desk keeps DeCamp as major Ukraine-adjacent foreign-policy wire even when lead package is ME/Africa — scan for Ukraine bullets each morning.

items.headline: Judging Freedom: INTEL roundtable w/ Larry Johnson & Joe Kent (week wrap)
items.summary: Napolitano week-wrap intel panel — desk watches for Ukraine/Russia threads among ME items; Mercouris regularly cites this guest circle.

items.headline: TF Rodovka / Rybar EN: 'Costly Affair' — strike campaign vs Ukrainian economy
items.summary: Named maps desk (TF Rodovka); seed from Rybar in English digest arguing concrete figures on effectiveness of strikes against Ukrainian economic/energy targets. Use Rodovka posts when fetchable; else Rybar-related Telegram war maps.

items.headline: WSJ: Ukraine fires hard-to-stop ballistic missile for first time
items.summary: Major WSJ headline only (desk exception): Ukraine's first reported use of a hard-to-intercept ballistic missile — capability note, not full WSJ reprint.

items.headline: Sonar21: Russia is not collapsing — reply to Con Coughlin
items.summary: Pushback on Telegraph-style “Russia collapsing” copy — desk keeps Sonar21 as the anti-Atlanticist force/narrative check alongside AMK maps and TASS wires.

items.headline: The Duran: Russia's sky campaign isolating Kiev and Odessa
items.summary: Mercouris/Christoforou: methodical isolation of Kyiv — ports, rail, internet/comms — compared to 1991 Iraq air campaign; pressure on Odessa logistics and capital livability.

items.headline: Sonar21: Europe defense-plant fires — what they mean for Ukraine
items.summary: Johnson on European defense-industrial incidents as a rear-area signal while the Ukraine proxy consumes munitions NATO cannot replace at wartime tempo.

items.headline: Duran Substack: Orekhov surrender leaflets; Kiev strikes; Lyman claims disputed
items.summary: Alex Christoforou/Mercouris: RU leaflets on Orikhiv pocket; central Kiev strikes; skepticism of Biletsky Lyman 'success'; rasputitsa risk; Geran-5 / Oreshnik rumors.

items.headline: Diesen × Larry Johnson: Europe–Russia war now “inevitable”?
items.summary: Sonar21’s Larry Johnson on Diesen’s show arguing European escalation paths toward direct confrontation with Russia as the Ukraine proxy strategy fails.

items.headline: Sonar21: Moscow closes the door — Putin/Lavrov harden Ukraine line
items.summary: Larry Johnson: ten-day hardening of Russian terms — no cheap ceasefire; West still selling pause narratives while Moscow prices in NATO as combatant/interlocutor.

items.headline: Ukraine front: three cauldrons & Trump's false hope w/ Krapivnik
items.summary: Stanislav Krapivnik on The Duran: multiple cauldron narratives on the Ukrainian front and skepticism toward ceasefire/peace framing from Washington.

items.headline: Diesen × Beebe: NATO lost Ukraine & Europe prepares for war
items.summary: Former CIA Russia analysis chief George Beebe with Diesen: Western strategy failing to weaken Russia; risk that capitals escalate rather than reassess — Provoked/Duran-adjacent realism.

items.headline: Diesen × Mercouris: Germany & Russia vote — Europe’s war fever
items.summary: Mercouris on Greater Eurasia with Diesen: European war fever, German/Russian political signals, and the Duran line that NATO euphoria flips to escalation panic as the attrition war turns.

items.headline: Antiwar: Ukraine launches 1,000+ drones in 'largest attack' on Moscow
items.summary: news.antiwar.com: Ukraine's mass drone strike framed as among the largest attacks aimed at Moscow/Russia deep rear — part of ongoing reciprocal energy/infrastructure campaign.

items.headline: Scott Horton Show: Ben Aris deep-dive on the state of the Ukraine war
items.summary: Horton interviews Ben Aris on Russian society, the evolving war, and barriers to peace — desk's recent long-form Ukraine interview on the Horton feed.

items.headline: Antiwar: energy-site attacks continue despite Trump 'stop' claim
items.summary: Dave DeCamp desk: Ukraine and Russia keep hitting energy sites after Trump claimed both sides agreed to halt such attacks — ceasefire narrative vs tape.
